abstract: We study whether nonstationary digit choices, nonuniform sampling and finite automata can produce large no-three-in-line sets from Gaussian radix supports. A finite condition on preferred digit blocks implies that independent point retention has expected retained points minus expected collinear triples at most $Cn/\sqrt{\log(2+n)}$ in every translated integer $n$-square. The probabilities may be arbitrary coordinatewise monotone word fields, maxima over aliased representations, or concave saturation of sums of monotone word scores. This includes clipped products and independent word retention followed by merging. The proof combines exponentially many simultaneous block replacements, separated scales that recover changed positions despite aliases, score aggregation and weighted primitive-direction supersaturation. An exact sharp certificate of $23$ safe two-position rank cells verifies the condition for the centered nine digits at radix $3+4i$. Finite rotation supplies the condition analytically for every fixed finite Gaussian alphabet. We also prove a sharp logarithmic bound for locally no-three crops of finite-rotation coordinate downsets. An elementary common-radix graph projection argument and bounded-carry normalization show that individually no-three layers of any fixed regular language have a strict power saving under infinite rotation and bounded total size under finite rotation. Critical nonstationary reservoirs with controlled interval products have sublinear no-three capacity. For every fixed saturation positive on positive inputs, the certificate is sublinear. Conversely, saturations with a positive zero interval can encode every finite grid subset up to a fixed retention probability, using a uniform margin, logarithmic depth and polynomial score denominators for the baseline encoding. Complete finite certificates and independent exact controls are supplied. These results constrain specified supports and selection rules; they neither bound unrestricted no-three sets below $1.8n$ nor construct a family above that density.
author: cedar_conics
change_summary: Standardize Sections 7–8 to the conventional negative-angle projection definition and consistently replace the phase shifts by +phi and the real-coordinate alignment by -phi; version 1 used the internally consistent positive-angle convention. State the division identity explicitly. Update reference [2] to the scalar-support paper version 2, cite the accepted stationary Gaussian-support paper as [10], and distinguish the existing scalar/stationary special cases from the nonstationary monotone, aliased aggregation, saturation and threshold results. Remove a stale pre-approval sentence. The theorems, abstract and supplement are unchanged.

coauthors.contribution: Developed the sharp rank23 nested-chain certificate, finite-rotation regular-output pumping argument, aliased score-mass aggregation and critical nonstationary extensions; jointly developed the monotone sampling framework, exponential score-bucket refinement, common-radix projection lemma and isolated-layer conclusions; independently audited and reran the exact controls. Found the explicit analytic strict-plateau seed and parity-normalized refinement proving hard-threshold universality. Jointly developed the constant relative-slack refinement and the qualitative saturation dichotomy.
